steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Line a 9x13-inch pan with greased parchment paper.
Place sugar, cocoa, flour, melted butter, eggs, vanilla, and salt in a large bowl. Mix until well combined; it will be thick and sticky. Spread brownie batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Cool completely; cut into squares and dust with confectioners’ sugar.

raw_recipe.headline: Chewiest Brownies
raw_recipe.description: Looking for the best chewy brownie recipe? These deliciously rich, fudgy, chocolaty brownies are irresistible and incredibly easy to make!
raw_recipe.name: Chewiest Brownies

review.reviewBody: Wow! Best brownie recipe ever! I followed the advice of some other users: Decreased the cocoa powder to 3/4C, decreased the sugar to 1 1/2C and increased the melted butter to 3/4C. Also, to help with the mixing so it doesnt get crumbly, melt the butter really well and then add the sugar, vanilla and eggs. In a seperate bowl mix the rest of the dry ingredients. Now mix the two together. Mixing the indregients this way (rather than putting them all in a single bowl and mixing as the recipe says) will make the batter easier to mix and spread.

I like experimenting with brownie recipes and this one is for sure a keeper. I decrerased cocoa to 3/4 cup and sugar to 1 1/2 cup, increased butter to 3/4 cup. I softened the butter(Did NOT melt) and wisked that in a bowl with the cocoa so it looked like melted chocolate.Then wisked in the sugar,eggs and vanilla, Then stirred in the flour and salt. I do ALOT of baking and all the good brownie recipes usually get handmixed in that order. The only thing I would do different is bake in a square pan, They were awful thin. I like my brownies thick. Thanks for the good recipe!!!

Made a few changes according to comments and my preference and these were absolute warm chewy chocolatey heaven, especially in my brownie sundae!!! Use 1 cup sugar (I used half dark brown, half light brown because that's all I had); 3/4 cup cocoa; 1/4 cup vegetable oil (in addition to listed butter). I also followed my tastes and added plenty of chocolate chips and candied pecans (pecans toasted in butter and brown sugar). Finally, I cooked in 8x8 pan so brownies are nice and thick. I overcooked them the first time -- 300F for 1 hour in an 8x8 is too much, they were dry. This time I did 300F for 25 minutes and 275F for 35 minutes and they were perfect! The center was 158F when I took it out which is about the safe temp to cook things containing eggs. Absolutely delicious!!!

Best chewy brownie recipe ever! I did as other reviewers suggested and decreased the cocoa powder to 3/4 cup and sugar to 1 1/2 cup (I did 3/4 c white sugar and 3/4 c brown sugar). I baked mine in a 9" pie pan at 300 for 40-45 minutes and they were PERFECT!

I made these tonight and they were perfect! Super chewy, chocolatey goodness! Prior to cooking, I read some of the other reviews, and made a couple alterations. I decreased the amount of sugar to 3/4 cup and the cocoa to 3/4 cup. In addition to the other listed ingredients I added 1/4 cup coconut oil. I only greased the pan, did not use wax paper. I’m at a very high elevation so they only needed about 27-28 mins on 300 degrees. I let them cool on a rack for 15 mins. Cut & served w/ confections sugar. Delicious and super easy! Will be making them often LOL

i think there should be more emphasis on how thick this batter actually is. I had a hard time getting it evenly into the pan, so i ended up going for an 8×8 instead. they cooked well, and didn't take the full 30 minutes for me. they were not cakey at all!

In my quest for chewy brownies, I came upon this recipe. I prefer chewy, not cakey brownies. This recipe delivers. I did take other reviewers' suggestions by decreasing the cocoa powder to 1/2 cup and decreasing the sugar to 1 1/2 cups. Definately chewy. Dough is sticky, so I added a splash of milk and lined an 8x8 pan with parchment and spread mixture on top. Next time, I will double recipe. Not the prettiest, but definately the tastiest & chewiest recipe I've ever tried. Outside crust is crackly and slightly crisp. I may try pouring chocholate ganache over the top next time. Yummy!
I liked the simplicity of the recipe however as suggested I added an extra egg because the batter wasn’t sticky enough. I topped it off with cream cheese icing.

If you’re like me and started to make this recipe and quickly realized there isn’t enough liquid and there’s no way this will work, here’s how you can fix it. Add another 1/2 cup of butter and another egg, bake at 350 for 22 minutes in a 9x13 pan. Even the fixed version I made isn’t the best brownie ever but it’s edible at least!

I used this recipe to make brownie cups. I patted these into 18 well greased muffin tins and baked at 350 for 22 minutes. They came out perfectly. Add a scoop of ice cream, chocolate sauce and a cherry and you have a decadent brownie sundae that is beautiful and yummy. It was a hit with my kids and pretty enough for guests. This recipe lives up to the "chewy" part. And its also really chocolatey. I cut back on cocoa powder, as suggested, and added flour so that the dry ingredients stayed at 2 cups. I did not cut back on the sugar, but should have. They were super sweet. That's why I could only give it 4 stars. I'm not sure these would make good stand-alone brownies, but this recipe was perfect for my use.

These came out very good, chewy and moist, just right for a thin fudge-like brownie! I only gave it 4 stars because I did lower the amount of cocoa powder to 3/4 C and the sugar to 1 1/2 C. I mixed it in one bowl just fine. It is very thick to spread, but it worked out okay. I baked it in a glass pyrex 9X13 dish lined with aluminum foil at 300 for 45 minutes.
they came out more like fudge than brownies. Set up quite hard.
My family said they were the best I ever made
I love these brownies. The only changes are that I add 1 cup of walnuts and use an 8 x 8 pan, which makes them gooey and divine.
Flavor fell flat. Tasted like it was missing something

The oven temperature in the recipe is wrong. Baking the brownies at only 300 degrees leads them to be far underdone . The 1st time I made the recipe, the brownies turned out very nice. The 2nd and 3rd times they were a gooey, underdone mess. This last time I cooked them for an additional 25 minutes trying to get them to bake. I have decided that the 1st time I made the recipe, I must have accidently set the oven temperature to 350. That's why the brownies turned out well the 1st time, but only the 1st time. Baking them at 300 does NOT work. Please revise this recipe. Every other chewy brownie recipe I have seen calls for a standard 350 degree oven!
I didn't deviate from the recipe at all. The brownies turned out amazing! They were so fudgy and chewy;not cake-like at all! I was very pleased and will definitely make them again.

In order to make this recipe work we had to add another 1/4 cup of butter and 1/8 cup of heavy cream, otherwise it was so thick you couldn't pour it in the pan. Now we have chewy brownies, but the recipe without modification is unusable.

I felt like the dough was much too stiff and hard to spread across the bottom of the pan. I might use a 7" x 11" pan if I make it again. I had to find a brownie recipe because I didn't have a box mix for a spur of the moment event, too short a notice to take a cake to church potluck.
Pretty darned good. The thickness of the batter made it quite a challenge to get it spread on greased parchment paper. The brownies are delicious and high in chocolate content.
